title: Circuit growth and subspace read-out in quantum-selected configuration interaction: Separating the Hartree-Fock determinant
authors: Ayaka Fujimoto, Norifumi Matsumoto, Shota Kanasugi, Kazunori Maruyama, Hirotaka Oshima
abstract: Predicting many molecular properties requires accurate ground-state energies of molecular Hamiltonians. Quantum-selected configuration interaction (QSCI) obtains such energies by measuring an input state to select important electronic configurations and classically diagonalizing the Hamiltonian in the subspace they span. ADAPT-QSCI, an adaptive extension of QSCI, improves the input state through iterative circuit growth. For single-reference molecules, the sampling distribution is dominated by the Hartree-Fock (HF) configuration, so most measurements reproduce a configuration already known. We reduce this redundancy by placing the HF configuration in the diagonalization subspace classically, before any measurement. This invalidates the operator-selection criterion of ADAPT-QSCI, and we derive a consistent replacement with energy and gradient in closed form, adding no query to the quantum device. At the per-iteration shot budgets previously used for ADAPT-QSCI, the proposed scheme reaches chemical accuracy with approximately $63\%$ and $43\%$ of the CNOT gates for $\mathrm{H}_4$ and $\mathrm{H}_6$, and $44\%$ and $40\%$ of the total shots. The advantage depends on the budget, however: in the infinite-shot limit the $\mathrm{H}_4$ CNOT count increases to $125\%$ of that of ADAPT-QSCI. These results identify the per-iteration shot budget as a key design variable governing resource savings in QSCI-based algorithms.
summary: This paper improves the Quantum-selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI) algorithm by recognizing and removing measurement redundancy caused by the dominant Hartree-Fock configuration. By classically supplying the HF determinant, the authors derive a more efficient selection criterion. The results show significant resource savings in terms of quantum circuit depth and measurement shots compared to existing adaptive methods for calculating molecular ground-state energies.
main_problem: Predicting accurate ground-state energies of molecular Hamiltonians, which is central to electronic structure theory.
main_result: The proposed scheme achieves chemical accuracy with significantly fewer CNOT gates and fewer measurement shots compared to ADAPT-QSCI at comparable shot budgets.
method: The authors modify the Quantum-selected Configuration Interaction (QSCI) approach by classically incorporating the Hartree-Fock determinant into the diagonalization subspace, thereby reducing measurement redundancy.
model_or_system: The study focuses on molecular Hamiltonians, specifically applied to small hydrogen molecules ($\mathrm{H}_4$ and $\mathrm{H}_6$), using electronic structure theory concepts.
key_observables: Ground-state energy, CNOT gate count, total measurement shots, and the required number of iterations ($k^*$) to reach chemical accuracy.
important_parameters: The per-iteration shot budget ($N_s$) is identified as a key design variable governing resource savings; the comparison's advantage depends on this budget.
main_assumptions: The advantage of the new scheme is contingent on the per-iteration shot budget, and the comparison is made assuming no device noise.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically compares the circuit structure of the proposed scheme against ADAPT-QSCI, highlighting added and inherited gates.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the redundancy in standard QSCI/ADAPT-QSCI methods due to the HF determinant. It then proposes the classical separation of the HF determinant and derives a new, consistent selection criterion. Finally, it compares the resource costs (gates/shots) against ADAPT-QSCI for $\mathrm{H}_4$ and $\mathrm{H}_6$.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource scaling and algorithmic efficiency for simulating strongly correlated electronic systems, which is a major bottleneck in quantum chemistry.
